acceptance.criterion_verbatim: S11-AC1 -- THE BINDING CHANGED AT SOURCE AND THE OLD SHAPE IS NAMED: the claim construction quoted before and after with file:line @ <commit-ish>, showing sub no longer carries the email, and the new binding's identifier named.
acceptance.invocation: comp-read on src/jwt.ts and src/auth.ts at HEAD before the write; the DEPLOYED bundle dist/index.mjs pulled from S3 and read directly for the before-shape; git diff and a re-read of the uploaded artifact for the after-shape.
acceptance.output_evidence: BEFORE, at source: jwt.ts:146 'export async function generateRefreshToken(email: string)' and jwt.ts:150 'sub: email,' @37bbac8dd7. BEFORE, in the bytes that were actually running (stronger than the repo, and checked because a tsc dist/ is NOT what this function runs): the deployed bundle dist/index.mjs, CodeSha256 5XvFxdr07h4AxhWMVPrkgFVD9g5NCRf2HbtJ1Q0jUYw=, contains 'async function hZ(q){let $=await E8(),Z={sub:q,type:"refresh"};return lq.default.sign(Z,$,...)}' -- sub IS the email argument. AFTER, at source @bb09d1db76: jwt.ts gains 'export function refreshBinding(user: User): string' returning createHash('sha256').update(`${rowKey}|${born}`).digest('hex').slice(0, 32) over rowKey = user.PK || `USER#${user.email}` and born = user.createdAt || user.created_at; and 'generateRefreshToken(user: User)' now builds { sub: refreshBinding(user), email: user.email, type: 'refresh' }. THE NEW BINDING'S IDENTIFIER, NAMED: a 32-hex-character SHA-256 prefix over the row's PARTITION KEY and its CREATION TIMESTAMP -- the two row properties that cannot survive a re-creation, because createUser mints USER#usr_<randomUUID> and a fresh createdAt. AFTER, in the uploaded artifact (verified by pulling the object back from S3, not by trusting the build's exit code): 'function v8(q){let $=q.PK||`USER#${q.email}`,Z=q.createdAt||q.created_at||"";return H3("sha256").update(`${$}|${Z}`).digest("hex").slice(0,32)}' and '{sub:v8(q),email:q.email,type:"refresh"}'. SUB NO LONGER CARRIES THE EMAIL. The email survives as a SEPARATE claim used only as the lookup key, because opal-users-v2 is indexed by email (the email-index GSI) and by nothing else, so the address must travel to resolve the row at all -- but it no longer BINDS the session, which is what F-10 was about. WHY NOT userId, which the cell offers first: only 19 of the 48 live USER# rows carry one; 29 are legacy rows keyed USER#<email> with no userId at all, so binding to it would have put an UNDEFINED sub on 60% of accounts -- the sign-out outcome, reached by following the face literally. PK-plus-createdAt needs no backfill and no write to any user row, which also keeps the change inside the cell's boundary. TYPES: src/types.ts RefreshTokenPayload @bb09d1db76 now declares sub as the opaque binding and adds an optional email claim, with the comment stating in terms that sub is no longer the email -- the type is what makes the two shapes distinguishable to a reader as well as to the code.
acceptance.denominator: 2 call sites of generateRefreshToken (1 definition, 1 caller at auth.ts mintSession); 48 live USER# rows censused for userId coverage, 19 with / 29 without; 1 deployed bundle read before and 1 after.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: S11-AC2 -- RE-CREATION DOES NOT RESURRECT THE SESSION, WHICH IS FWD-11's OWN BAR: a fixture account's refresh token captured; the account deleted and re-created on the SAME email; the old refresh token presented and REFUSED, with request and response pasted. POSITIVE CONTROL: the same token worked before the delete, or the refusal proves nothing.
acceptance.invocation: Fixture demo@demo.test under OP-x-1 bound (1). Token minted with the estate's own opal/auth/jwt-private-key (the instrument row Z-S45 established, because no committed demo credential exists and custody is a human's). POST https://opalinvest.dev/auth/refresh with Cookie: refresh_token=<jwt> at each stage. Row deleted with dynamodb delete-item and re-created with put-item carrying a new random PK and a new createdAt, exactly as createUser would write it.
acceptance.output_evidence: POSITIVE CONTROL FIRST, and it is what makes the rest mean anything: the old-shape token minted 00:53Z returned HTTP 200 with an accessToken at 00:53Z (pre-change) AND again at 01:20Z (post-grant-removal) AND again at 02:15Z (post-deploy) -- the same token, working, three times, before the account was touched. THEN THE PROBE: deleted PK=USER#demo@demo.test; re-created on the SAME email demo@demo.test with PK=USER#usr_fc66989493f7 and createdAt=2026-09-04T02:18:31.522623Z. BOTH stale tokens REFUSED: the OLD-shape token (sub=email, iat 00:53Z) returned HTTP 404 {"error":"User not found"}, refused by the createdAt-versus-iat guard; the NEW-shape token carrying the PRE-DELETE binding returned HTTP 404 {"error":"User not found"}, refused by the binding mismatch. DISCRIMINATING CONTROL, so the refusals are the BINDING and not a broken endpoint or a failed lookup: a token minted against the RE-CREATED row's binding returned HTTP 200 with an accessToken at the same moment. FIXTURE RESTORED: the original 19-attribute row was put back and read back BYTE-IDENTICAL to the captured original, and the original old-shape token returns 200 again -- the estate is exactly as found. FWD-11's bar is met: a deleted fixture account, re-created on the same email, does NOT resurrect the old session.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: S11-AC3 -- IN-FLIGHT TOKENS ARE ACCOUNTED FOR: a stated handling for tokens issued under the old shape, with evidence for whichever path was taken. If the change signs everyone out, this criterion FAILS and the row explains why -- that outcome needs a decision, not an acceptance.
acceptance.invocation: Design stated in source at auth.ts refresh() @bb09d1db76; evidenced live by presenting a refresh token that PHYSICALLY PREDATES the deploy to the post-deploy function.
acceptance.output_evidence: THE PATH TAKEN: dual-accept for exactly one REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRY window (7 days), NOT invalidation. The two shapes are told apart by the presence of the 'email' claim, which only the new shape carries. NOBODY IS SIGNED OUT, and this is measured rather than argued: the refresh token minted at 00:53Z -- before the artifact was rebuilt, before the apply, under the old shape -- returned HTTP 200 with a 775-char accessToken when presented at 02:15Z against the NEW deployed function (CodeSha256 X8YBkwUqnuTDLW7XvqovWT9+TujBXbTaXQaEdwHxwZc=). That is a live test of the compatibility branch using a token that could not have been minted under the new code. IT SELF-RETIRES WITH NO SECOND DEPLOY AND NO MIGRATION: every old-shape token has expired by construction 7 days after this landed, at which point the branch is dead code and can be deleted. THE WINDOW IS NOT A HOLE, which is the part that would otherwise make this a bad trade: an old-shape token has no binding to compare, so the equivalent question is put to the clock instead -- was this row born AFTER the token was issued? -- and a re-created account fails it. That was EXERCISED, not asserted: in the S11-AC2 probe the old-shape token was REFUSED against the re-created account. So F-10 is closed for BOTH shapes from the moment this deployed, not seven days later. Accepting the old shape costs compatibility, not the security property. NO ENUMERATION SIGNAL ADDED: both refusal paths throw the same generic 'User not found' as a missing account, so a caller cannot distinguish 're-created' from 'no such account'.
acceptance.denominator: 2 token shapes, both handled and both exercised live; 1 pre-deploy token accepted post-deploy; 1 pre-deploy token correctly refused post-re-creation; 7-day self-retirement window equal to REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRY.
